title: Readable, clean Java code
idea: Clean code is code a teammate can read once and change safely: names say intent, methods do one thing, and rules live in one obvious place.
points: Name variables and methods for what they mean, not their type.
Replace magic numbers and strings with named constants or an `enum`.
Use guard clauses to exit early instead of nesting `if` blocks.
Extract a condition into a small method whose name explains it.

hero.title: Same rule, two ways to write it

right.title: Easy to read
items: `costInPence(items, orderTotalPence, tier)` reads like a sentence
Constants such as `FREE_FROM_PENCE` name each number
`enum Tier` lets the compiler reject bad values
A guard clause, then one flat decision

hero.verdict: Both price valid orders the same; only one can be changed without fear.

code.title: Before
code.caption: It works, but every reader must decode the letters and numbers first.

walk.text: The signature tells you nothing: what are `n`, `t` and `c`?
Nesting hides the real rule: premium or big orders ship free.
A `-1` sentinel looks like a price; callers can add it by mistake.

code.title: After
code.caption: Same prices for valid orders; the empty order now fails loudly instead of returning a fake price.

walk.text: An `enum` replaces the strings, so a typo no longer compiles.
Each number gets a name and a unit, in one place.
A guard clause rejects bad input first and keeps the rest flat.
The whole rule now reads as one sentence.
A tiny private method names the free-shipping condition.

pitfalls: Do not abbreviate names to save typing; you read code far more than you write it.
Avoid comments that repeat the code; rename or extract a method instead.
Refactor in small steps and rerun the same inputs after each one.

quiz.q: Using `ShippingQuote` above, what does this print?
quiz.code:
ShippingQuote quote = new ShippingQuote();
System.out.println(quote.costInPence(3, 1000, Tier.STANDARD));
quiz.why: `qualifiesForFreeShipping` uses `>=`, and 1000 equals `FREE_FROM_PENCE`, so the method returns 0 before computing a price.

takeaway: Write code that explains itself: clear names, flat flow, small methods.

starters: How long should a method be before I split it?
When is a comment better than a clearer name?
How do I refactor messy code without breaking it?
